thesis: Figma is the dominant collaborative design platform with ~80-90% UI/UX market share, growing revenue at 40%+ (TTM $1.16B, +41.4%) with positive free cash flow and 130%+ net revenue retention. After cratering ~78% from post-IPO highs on SaaS multiple compression and AI-disruption anxiety, the stock has stabilized and rebounded off its $16.60 low as Q1 2026 results (+46% revenue growth, raised full-year outlook) eased fears that prompt-to-interface tools would make Figma redundant. At a mid-single-digit forward EV/Revenue with ~$1.6B cash and minimal debt, Figma trades at a discount to high-growth SaaS peers. Key risks: AI disruption, no GAAP profitability (-$1.40B net loss TTM), heavy stock-based dilution, and an activist campaign pressing for cost discipline.

drivers: FY2026 revenue beats the raised full-year outlook as AI credit monetization (Figma Make, Weave, Code Layers, AI agents) scales
Net revenue retention holds above 130% as enterprise customers expand seats and adopt new products
Q1 2026 momentum (+46% revenue growth) proves AI is a tailwind, not an existential threat, driving a SaaS multiple re-rate
Cost rationalization from the Findell activist campaign accelerates the path to GAAP profitability
Short-covering and scarcity premium for durable 40%+ growth at scale amplify upside on any beat

risks: Revenue growth decelerates toward 25% as AI-native tools (Claude Design, v0) erode share
Gross margins compress further below 80% due to rising AI compute costs
Stock-based compensation stays elevated, preventing GAAP profitability and diluting shareholders
Insider selling and lockup supply keep a persistent overhang on the stock
Broad SaaS multiple compression drags shares back toward the $16.60 52-week low

base_case.assumptions: Revenue grows 35-40% in FY2026 to roughly $1.45-1.55B; FCF margin stabilizes at 20-25%; SBC moderates as a share of revenue; company reaches EBITDA breakeven by 2027; stock trades at 8-10x forward EV/Revenue as the profitability path becomes visible — in line with the ~$31-33 analyst consensus.

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 Earnings — first report since Config 2026 and raised full-year outlook
Q3 2026 Earnings — durability check on AI credit monetization and NRR
General availability ramp of Config 2026 launches (Code Layers, Motion, AI agents)
Findell Capital activist campaign — cost rationalization and product-focus outcome

key_risks: AI disruption risk — AI-native design tools (Claude Design, v0) could commoditize Figma's core value proposition
No GAAP profitability with a -$1.40B TTM net loss; path to earnings remains uncertain
Gross margin compression from 91% (2023) to 82% (2025) — AI compute costs could pressure it further
Heavy stock-based-compensation dilution: diluted shares outstanding have climbed toward ~528M
Activist pressure (Findell Capital) signals investor frustration with cost structure and product focus
Recent IPO with limited trading history; lockup and insider-selling overhang may pressure the stock
SaaS sector multiple compression could persist if rates rise or recession fears intensify
